stage: Temporal Benchmark Validity Audit — Stage A

recommended_candidate_population.status: candidate population for chronological benchmark redesign; final split not yet selected

excluded_sparse_regime.reason: Pre-June-2025 observations are temporally sparse and originate from a substantially different source composition.

label_provenance.benchmark_use: Usable as an explicitly LLM-labeled supervised target with disclosure of annotation uncertainty.

source_structure.finding: The dense regime is strongly source-concentrated, with firstsquaw and WalterBloomberg accounting for approximately 95% of observations overall.
source_structure.implication: Source composition must be tracked as a temporal covariate and potential confounder when interpreting future performance degradation.

conditions: Describe Dataset B explicitly as LLM-labeled rather than human-gold annotated.
Report label uncertainty, especially neutral-versus-directional ambiguity.
Restrict the core chronological benchmark to the dense primary-source regime rather than using the sparse 565-observation early regime.
Track source/channel composition across chronological windows as a potential temporal confounder.
Select the final chronological split using timestamps and sample-support criteria only, not model performance.
Repeat the near-duplicate leakage check at the exact final train/test boundary.
approved_next_stage: Design the within-Dataset-B chronological train/validation/future-window benchmark.
not_approved_as_primary_temporal_evidenc: Dataset A -> Dataset B performance degradation, which remains external OOD robustness evidence.
